name: Zoho CRM

identity.note: Multi-datacenter product (zoho.com, .eu, .in, .com.au, .jp, etc.); OAuth and API domains vary by data center. Current API version is v8.

summary: Zoho CRM is a cloud CRM for managing leads, contacts, accounts, deals and sales automation, with a broad REST API.

auth.detail: OAuth 2.0. Register a client in the Zoho API Console (https://api-console.zoho.com/). Server-based, client-based, mobile and self-client types are available. Self Client suits a single org and needs no redirect URL. Access tokens last 1 hour. Refresh tokens last until revoked. Credentials are per data center.

gates: API credits are capped per 24-hour window by edition: Free 5,000; Standard/Starter 50k base, 100k max; Professional 3M max; Enterprise/Zoho One 5M max; Ultimate/CRM Plus unlimited.
Some endpoints and features depend on edition. I did not confirm which ones.
Credentials and API domains are per data center, so multi-region customers need region-aware OAuth.
The vendor's own MCP servers consume API credits like normal API calls.

resource_families: records (Leads, Contacts, Accounts, Deals, custom modules)
metadata (modules, fields, layouts, custom views, related lists)
api.note: v8 REST API with credit-based rate limits per 24-hour rolling window. Insert/update/upsert accept at most 100 records per call. COQL is an SQL-like query API. Composite API combines up to 5 calls in one request. Bulk APIs are asynchronous.

mcp.note: Zoho publishes four pre-built MCP servers: Data Insights (read-only COQL), Data Operations (CRUD), Module Customization, and Workflow & Process Automation. They use OAuth and work with Cursor, Claude Desktop, VS Code and Windsurf.

open_questions: Does a public multi-tenant OAuth app (server-based client) need Zoho review or marketplace listing? I found no evidence of one.
Is the API available on every paid edition? The API Limits page lists credits for all editions, including Free, so it likely is. Some edition-specific endpoint restrictions were not checked.
Does the Free Edition include full API access? Its 5,000-credit allowance suggests it does, but I did not confirm this on a pricing page.

name: Gorgias

summary: Gorgias is an ecommerce-focused customer support helpdesk with a REST API for tickets, customers and related data, plus an AI Agent and MCP server.

auth.detail: Private app: HTTP Basic auth with the account email as username and an API key created by an owner/admin in Settings > Account > REST API. Public app: OAuth2 authorization code flow, mandatory for public apps. Access tokens last 24 hours. The OAuth subdomain is per-account.

gates: A 7-day free trial is available with no credit card (cap of 10 email ticket messages, no help center publishing). The trial runs on a Helpdesk plan, so API key creation should work, but this was not explicitly confirmed on a trial account.
No free Gorgias plan exists; the helpdesk itself is paid (Starter from $10/month). The API is included on all Helpdesk plans with no separate API purchase or higher tier required.
The account owner or an admin creates the API key in Settings > Account > REST API.
OAuth2 is mandatory for public apps. The app must be approved by Gorgias before it appears in the in-product App Store.
Optional Sandbox/developer account needs a registered Developer Portal account and a draft app; new sandboxes are Demo accounts until Gorgias switches them to a Developer plan by email.
API keys are tied to an individual user's account and grant full access to the account's data.
Rate limits: 40 requests per 20 seconds for API keys, 80 per 20 seconds for OAuth2 apps.

api.note: REST API at {subdomain}.gorgias.com/api. Rate limits use a leaky bucket and the API returns 429 with Retry-After. Cursor pagination. Only some resource families were confirmed from the fetched docs sidebar (customers, custom fields, events, files, integrations, jobs, macros); the rest (tickets, messages, users, tags, etc.) come from general knowledge of the API.

mcp.note: Vendor-hosted Gorgias MCP is in open beta for all paid plan customers. Community servers also exist, e.g. benpalmer1/Gorgias-MCP-Server.

name: Zoho Cliq

identity.note: Zoho's team chat product. REST API v2 is documented, and a newer v3 is described as recommended for new integrations. Zoho data centers are region-specific (zoho.com, zoho.in, and others).

summary: Zoho Cliq is a team chat and collaboration platform with channels, direct and group chats, bots, meetings and reminders.

auth.detail: OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow. Register a client in the Zoho API Console (client types include server-based, client-based, mobile, non-browser and Self Client). Requests send 'Authorization: Zoho-oauthtoken <token>'. Scopes are granular, such as ZohoCliq.Channels.READ and ZohoCliq.Messages.READ. Access tokens last 1 hour and refresh tokens are used to get new ones. Token endpoints are domain-specific per Zoho data center.

gates: The Free plan is listed at no cost on the pricing page. A 14-day trial of paid plans is also offered.
The pricing page lists 'API support' as a feature, but the fetched text didn't make clear which plans include it. Treat API availability on the Free plan as likely but unconfirmed.
Documented rate limits are tight: the v2 docs list a quota of 5 requests per minute per user, and the Get Messages endpoint lists 15 requests per minute per user with a 5-minute lock period.
Org-wide export endpoints (OrganizationChats, OrganizationChannels, OrganizationMessages scopes) need org-admin level access.
OAuth endpoints are domain-specific, so multi-region customers need data-center-aware auth URLs.

api.note: REST API v2 is documented, and v3 is described as the recommended version for new integrations. An OpenAPI spec and a Postman collection are available. Rate limits are low: 5 requests per minute per user on one documented quota, and 15 requests per minute with a 5-minute lock on Get Messages. Bots, slash commands and webhooks come from the Cliq developer platform (Deluge).

mcp.note: Zoho publishes an official Cliq MCP server, set up through the Zoho MCP console (mcp.zoho.com), with Cliq tools covering bots, channels, messages, reminders and threads. Zoho documents connecting it to Claude, VS Code and other clients.

What are the exact current v3 rate limits? The v2 docs show low per-user quotas.
Do the OpenAPI and v3 docs list a different or larger endpoint set than v2?

name: Vonage

identity.note: Vonage Communications APIs (formerly Nexmo; Ericsson-owned). Distinct from Vonage Business Communications (UCaaS).

summary: Vonage provides cloud communications APIs for SMS, WhatsApp/RCS messaging, voice, video, number verification, and phone number management.

auth.detail: Account API key + secret (Basic auth or request params) from the Vonage dashboard; Applications have an application ID and private key used to sign RS256 JWTs (Messages, Voice, Video, etc.). No OAuth app model; credentials are per account.

The tooling server code is at github.com/Vonage-Community/vonage-mcp-server-api-bindings; it is run locally via npx, uses API key/secret plus application ID/private key, and covers SMS, WhatsApp, RCS, voice, numbers, reports and balance. gates: Starter tier is free (no charge, no payment method) but capped at 5 connections (tenant organisations) and 1,000 API calls per day per org. Enough for development and testing, not for serving many customers.

Serving more than 5 customer organisations requires a paid tier with a card on file: Core ($35 AUD/month, 50 connections), Plus ($245 AUD/month, 1,000 connections, requires App Certification), Advanced ($1,445 AUD/month, 10,000 connections, requires certification and security assessment), Enterprise (price on application).
Paid tiers also include egress allotments (Core 10 GB, Plus 50 GB, Advanced 250 GB) with overage at $2.40 AUD per GB.
Each Xero organisation can connect a maximum of five uncertified apps; there is no limit on certified apps, so broad distribution realistically needs App Certification.
Xero App Store listing needs Plus or above and is not available on Starter or Core.
Journals endpoint, Practice Manager (XPM) API and Bulk Connections need Advanced or above plus a security assessment and use-case approval.
The hosted Remote MCP server is Demo org only on Starter.
Custom Connections (client_credentials) cost a monthly fee on the Xero organisation, connect to one organisation only, and are available only for UK, AU, NZ and US orgs.
Some scopes are being deprecated for granular scopes; Custom Connections created from Apr 29, 2026 need the granular scopes.

api.note: Per-tenant limits: 5 concurrent calls, 60 per minute, 1,000 per day on Starter and 5,000 per day on Core and above. App-wide limit is 10,000 per minute. name: Discord

identity.note: Discord (chat and community platform). The API is mainly used through bot applications created in the Developer Portal.

summary: Discord is a chat and community platform whose developer API lets bots and apps send messages, manage servers and receive real-time events.

auth.detail: OAuth2 supports the authorization code grant, implicit grant and client credentials, plus special flows for bots and webhooks. Bots install into a guild through the `bot` scope and authenticate with a bot token from the Developer Portal Bot page. User-level OAuth2 scopes are limited to identity, guilds, connections and similar.

gates: Free developer signup: create an app in the Developer Portal, get a bot token, and install it to a test server (servers can be created for free).
Unverified bots can be in at most 100 servers at a time. Bots become eligible to apply for verification at 75 servers, so a public multi-tenant bot needs Discord verification to scale.

Privileged Intents (Guild Members, Presence, Message Content) can be self-toggled in the Developer Portal while the app reaches under 10,000 users. At 10,000+ users, Discord review and approval is required, with annual reapplication.
Some OAuth2 scopes (rpc, voice, dm_channels.read, identify.premium, applications.builds.upload) are only available to approved partners.
Reading user DMs and other user-level data is not available through normal OAuth2. Most server actions go through a bot token, which needs the bot installed in each customer's guild.
Heavy rate limiting applies. Apps that ignore rate limits can have their API keys revoked.

api.note: REST base URL is https://discord.com/api and the API is versioned. A WebSocket Gateway handles real-time events. Per-route rate limits apply, and Discord says clients that ignore them can be blocked.

mcp.note: Several community MCP servers exist (SaseQ, PaSympa, hanweg, others). They run with the user's own bot token. A third-party catalog lists an 'official' @discord/mcp-server. I could not verify that on any Discord-owned page, so I treat it as unverified.

blocker: Free to build and test. To serve many customers, a public bot must be verified by Discord once it passes 100 servers, and privileged intents such as Message Content need Discord review at 10,000+ users. The bot must also be installed in each customer's guild, and some scopes are partner-only.
open_questions: Is there a vendor-published official Discord MCP server? A third-party catalog claims one, but no Discord-owned page confirms it.

Apps can also redirect a merchant to /wc-auth/v1/authorize, which POSTs the generated keys back to the app's callback URL. WordPress Application Passwords are used for the MCP endpoint.

The MCP integration is in developer preview and needs the separate MCP Adapter plugin plus a WordPress Application Password.

api.note: REST API v3 at /wp-json/wc/v3/. Default pagination is 10 items per page. X-WP-Total and Link headers are returned. Official JS, PHP, Python and Ruby libraries exist. name: Salesforce Commerce Cloud

identity.note: Salesforce Commerce Cloud covers B2C Commerce (SCAPI/OCAPI, SLAS, Account Manager) and B2B Commerce on the core platform. This record covers B2C Commerce, which the hint docs and the SCAPI guides describe. SCAPI is also called the Salesforce Commerce API.

summary: Salesforce B2C Commerce is an enterprise ecommerce platform whose SCAPI REST APIs cover shopper storefront and admin/merchant operations.

auth.detail: Two token paths. Shopper APIs use SLAS, a Shopper Login and API Access Service. A SLAS public or private client is created in the SLAS Admin UI or API, and a private client has a secret. Admin APIs use an Account Manager API client with client ID and secret and allowed scopes, via OAuth2 client credentials. The client needs the Salesforce Commerce API role for specific instances. Each client is per tenant, with its own realm, instance, short code and org ID. OCAPI is a legacy alternative and needs its own separate API client.

gates: No self-serve developer signup or free developer sandbox was found. A developer needs a B2C Commerce instance, obtained via a licensed tenant. On-demand sandboxes need purchased sandbox credits via the Account Executive, and the realm ID comes from the AE or CSM.
The docs offer a shared public demo sandbox, but only for read-only Shopper API trials. It does not provide developer credentials.

Trailhead notes that B2C Commerce is not available in the Trailhead Playground; customer or partner developers are directed to ask their manager for sandbox access. No documented self-serve partner sandbox was found.

An Account Manager Account Administrator must create the API client and assign the Salesforce Commerce API role and organization/instance filters. The admin must also grant the SLAS Organization Administrator role to create SLAS clients.
The API is included for B2C Commerce customers at no extra cost, but each customer gets credentials only from their own tenant. There is no single multi-tenant public app.
Shopper and admin scopes must not be mixed on the same client. SCAPI clients and OCAPI clients must be separate. Account Manager client secrets must be alphanumeric.
Tokens are issued per instance, with one instance per token request.

api.note: SCAPI has Shopper APIs (SLAS tokens) and Admin APIs (Account Manager tokens), with 14+ admin API families. OCAPI is the legacy API. Requests need the org ID (f_ecom_<realm>_<instance>) and short code in the base URL. There is a Commerce SDK and a B2C CLI. Rate limits and quotas were not checked. Webhooks were not verified.

mcp.note: The official B2C DX MCP server (@salesforce/b2c-dx-mcp) runs locally. It is for developer workflows: SCAPI schema discovery, cartridge deployment, MRT and storefront development. It is not a general merchant-data tool. Salesforce also documents a hosted B2C Commerce MCP Service for agentic shopper tools, which is in pilot.

Dev credentials and sandboxes require a licensed tenant and purchased sandbox credits through a Salesforce Account Executive. Each customer's Account Manager admin must then create an API client or SLAS client. No central OAuth app exists.

identity.note: Covers Magento Open Source, Adobe Commerce (PaaS/on-prem/Cloud) and Adobe Commerce as a Cloud Service (SaaS). Each merchant has its own store host, so there is no single shared API endpoint for PaaS/Open Source.

summary: Adobe Commerce (formerly Magento) is an ecommerce platform exposing REST, GraphQL and SOAP APIs for catalog, orders, customers and more.

auth.detail: PaaS/on-prem/Open Source: a merchant admin creates an Integration, which issues consumer key/secret and access token/secret for OAuth 1.0a signing. summary: Neo4j is a graph database platform (self-managed or Aura cloud) queried with Cypher, with a cloud management API and per-database HTTP Query API and drivers.

auth.detail: Aura API: client ID/secret created in the Aura Console (Client credentials page) are exchanged for a 1-hour Bearer token via the OAuth 2.0 client_credentials grant at api.neo4j.io/oauth/token (token endpoint uses HTTP Basic with client ID/secret). This is a machine-to-machine flow, not a third-party multi-tenant authorization-code app model. Database access (Query API/Bolt) uses database username/password, or SSO bearer tokens on Enterprise/Aura.

gates: Aura API credentials can be created on all Aura tiers
Aura API rate limit is 25 req/min for Free and Pro trial without billing, 125 req/min for paid tiers
Billing endpoints limited to 10 requests/day per organization
Query API disabled by default on self-managed versions < 5.25 and needs enabling
Each customer must supply their own instance URI and credentials

api.note: Aura API v1 at https://api.neo4j.io, 45s timeout, rate limits by tier. Query API (HTTP, Cypher) introduced in 5.19 supersedes the deprecated HTTP API. Official drivers plus an Aura CLI exist.

mcp.note: Official neo4j/mcp (Go) with tools get-schema, read-cypher, write-cypher, list-gds-procedures. It supports stdio and HTTP modes. Neo4j also maintains mcp-neo4j-cypher and an Aura API MCP server in neo4j-contrib.

open_questions: Resource family list for the Aura API is from prior pass and not re-verified against the API spec.
MCP release/version details were not re-verified in this pass.

name: Datadog

identity.note: Multi-site SaaS (US1, US3, US5, EU, AP1, AP2, UK1, GovCloud); API base URL differs per site.

summary: Datadog is a cloud observability and security platform for metrics, logs, traces, monitors, dashboards and incidents, with a broad public API.

auth.detail: Customer's own account: org-level API key (writes/submits data) plus an application key (reads; tied to a user or service account, optionally scoped), both created in Organization Settings. Newer standalone Personal Access Tokens (ddpat_) and Service Access Tokens (ddsat_) need no API key pairing. OAuth2 authorization code (with PKCE) exists, but only for approved Technology Partners building official integrations via the Developer Platform; standalone OAuth clients are not supported. Requests must go to the customer's Datadog site. The hosted MCP server uses OAuth.

gates: Developer needs a Datadog account; the pricing page offers a free trial, after which you can move to a Free tier (up to five Basic hosts, 1-day metric retention) or a paid plan.
Not verified in docs: whether the Free tier (post-trial) includes API/application key access or which endpoints need paid products (e.g. logs, security, incident management).
Customers create their own API key and application key (or PAT) in Organization Settings, which requires appropriate permissions.

OAuth2 is limited to approved Technology Partners via the Datadog Partner Network and Developer Platform; OAuth can only be tested in a partner developer organization until Datadog publishes the integration. Standalone OAuth clients are not supported.
Customers must supply their Datadog site, because the API host differs per site.
Some APIs (App Builder, Actions Connections, Workflow Automation) need Actions API access enabled on the application key.
Endpoint rate limits vary and can be raised through Datadog support.
The hosted MCP server is not GovCloud compatible.

api.note: Available in v1 and v2, with per-site base URLs. Many endpoints are rate limited (429 plus X-RateLimit-* headers). Limits can be raised through support. Datadog says application keys become legacy features after Q3 2026 in favour of scoped credentials, but will keep working.

mcp.note: Official hosted remote MCP server from Datadog, documented on docs.datadoghq.com. Repo: github.com/datadog-labs/mcp-server (seen in search results, not fetched). Not GovCloud compatible.

blocker: Free-tier API access is unconfirmed. OAuth2 is restricted to approved Technology Partners, so general toolkits would rely on API key + application key or PATs.

name: Jira

identity.note: Assessed Jira Cloud platform REST API v3. Jira Software / Service Management / Align have additional APIs; Data Center/Server use different auth.

summary: Jira Cloud is Atlassian's issue and project tracking product, with a REST API for issues, projects, users, workflows and more.

auth.detail: OAuth 2.0 authorization code (3LO) apps created in the developer console are the recommended route for multi-site integrations, with rotating refresh tokens (offline_access scope). Basic auth with account email plus API token works for scripts but Atlassian discourages apps from collecting API tokens. Forge (OAuth) and Connect (JWT) apps are also supported.

gates: Atlassian says apps that collect API tokens or tell customers to create their own 3LO apps don't comply with its security requirements, so API tokens are not a viable route for a multi-tenant product. A single distributable 3LO app is the recommended route.
A 3LO app is private by default; sharing must be enabled in the developer console Distribution settings, and the authorization link is sent to users.

Shared 3LO apps show users a warning that Atlassian hasn't reviewed them until the integration is approved. Approval goes through the Marketplace listing process, and an informative Marketplace listing is not required to submit. The review is not a hard block, but its timeline is unknown.

Rate limits: points-based hourly quota (65,000 points/hour in the default shared Global Pool across all tenants), per-second burst limits per endpoint, and per-issue write limits. These are enforced for 3LO apps from March 2, 2026. HTTP 429 with Retry-After is returned.
Rotating refresh tokens expire after 90 days of inactivity, so users must re-authorize.
Apps can only do what the authenticated user's Jira permissions allow.

Developers can get a free cloud development site via the Cloud Developer Bundle. Whether the REST API is available on every customer plan (including Free) was not confirmed in official docs; community answers say most endpoints work on free sites.

api.note: OAuth 3LO calls go to api.atlassian.com/ex/jira/<cloudId>/rest/api/3/. Basic auth calls go to the site URL. Rich text fields use Atlassian Document Format. Rate limits: three independent systems (hourly points quota, per-second burst per endpoint per tenant, per-issue write limits); the default shared pool is 65,000 points/hour, and apps with very high usage may be moved to per-tenant pools after review.

mcp.note: The Atlassian Rovo MCP Server is hosted by Atlassian. It uses OAuth 2.1 or an API token for headless auth, and covers Jira, Confluence, JSM, Bitbucket and Loom. Repo: github.com/atlassian/atlassian-mcp-server. The overview page mentions Rovo credit usage, but the details were not read.

open_questions: Is the Jira REST API available on every customer plan including Free? Only community statements were found, not an official plan matrix.
How long does Atlassian's Marketplace approval of a shared 3LO integration take, and what are its exact criteria?
Will the shared 65,000 points/hour Global Pool be enough for a multi-tenant toolkit at scale, or will it need a quota review?

identity.note: Intuit also has QuickBooks Payments, Payroll and Desktop APIs; this assessment covers the QuickBooks Online Accounting API on developer.intuit.com.

summary: QuickBooks Online is Intuit's cloud accounting software, and its developer platform exposes accounting data (invoices, customers, bills, reports and so on) through an OAuth 2.0-secured API.

auth.detail: OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow. Create an app in the Intuit Developer Portal to get Client ID/Secret. Users authorize per QuickBooks company (realmId). Access tokens last 60 minutes and refresh tokens are rotated. Separate Development (sandbox) and Production keys.

gates: Production keys require completing Intuit's app assessment questionnaire, which Intuit reviews before approval. This applies to private, unlisted apps too.
Annual security assessment for all apps on the platform.

Intuit App Partner Program (US launch July 2025; UK/AU/CA from Nov 2025): every app is auto-enrolled at the Builder tier, which has no fee but is capped at 500,000 CorePlus (data-read) API credits per month; calls above the cap are blocked, not billed. Silver/Gold/Platinum charge a monthly program fee plus variable CorePlus overage fees.
Core (create/update) API calls are unmetered and uncharged on all tiers. CorePlus (reads, queries, reports) are metered. Apps that read heavily may need a paid tier.
Builder-tier apps listed on the Intuit App Marketplace are subject to delisting unless they subscribe to Silver. Some premium APIs (e.g. Workforce API) are available only to Silver and above.
Production OAuth redirect URIs must be public HTTPS (localhost is rejected).
Development keys work only with sandbox companies; production keys are separate.
Some features depend on the customer's QBO tier (Simple Start/Essentials/Plus/Advanced) or settings such as multi-currency.
Payments API and regulated industries have extra requirements.

api.note: REST with JSON is the main surface; Intuit docs also list a GraphQL option, but its entity coverage was not verified. Supports batch operations, change data capture, sparse updates and webhooks. The docs say the SDKs are only for OAuth 2.0 and QuickBooks Online, and some (e.g. Node) are OAuth client libraries, so full QBO API wrapper coverage per language is not verified. Since the 2025 Intuit App Partner Program, reads are metered: the Builder tier is capped at 500,000 CorePlus credits/month with excess calls blocked, and paid tiers bill overage. Create/update calls are unmetered. Per-tier fee numbers were not verified.

mcp.note: Intuit publishes an open-source local (stdio) MCP server in its own GitHub org, with 145 tools covering 29 entities and 11 reports. Search results also showed an Intuit-hosted MCP endpoint (mcp.quickbooks.intuit.com) under an AI pilot and an Intuit Claude connector; those pages were not fetched, so their access terms are unverified.

blocker: Free sandbox and a documented API are available, but production keys need Intuit's app assessment questionnaire and approval plus an annual security review. Under the Intuit App Partner Program, the free Builder tier caps data-read (CorePlus) calls at 500,000 per month and blocks calls above that. Heavier apps need a paid Silver or higher tier.
open_questions: Exact monthly fees and per-1,000-call overage rates per tier (on Intuit's platform-service-fees help article and partners/benefits page) were not fetched.
Does a customer need an active QBO subscription for production use? The FAQ defines active connections as companies with an active subscription, but no explicit API-gating statement was found.
GraphQL entity coverage in QBO was not verified.
Per-language SDK scope (full QBO API wrapper vs OAuth-only client) was not verified.
Access terms of the Intuit-hosted MCP endpoint are unverified.
